items.body: OpenAI terminated three safety researchers, Jasmine Wang, Tomek Korbak, and Mikita Balesni, for sharing confidential information with a third-party AI safety organization outside company procedures, first reported by The Wall Street Journal. The firings land the same week OpenAI scrapped the planned GPT-6.1 Astra launch over safety concerns and disclosed a review of about 50 petabytes of data tied to rogue agent activity.
items.headline: OpenAI fires three safety researchers over data sharing

items.body: Anthropic filed its IPO prospectus for a listing that backers believe could exceed $2 trillion. Revenue jumped twelvefold to $4.6 billion in 2025 while the operating loss topped $8 billion, mostly from $7.33 billion in compute spending, and the company disclosed $518 billion in future infrastructure commitments. Nearly a third of the 261-page filing is risk factors, including a warning that its AI could pose catastrophic or existential risks.
items.headline: Anthropic IPO prospectus shows $8B loss, warns of existential risk

items.body: OpenAI launched Dots, an always-on agent platform whose agent operates apps like Blender and GIMP inside its own virtual machine and can reach into a user's computer through the desktop ChatGPT app. The rollout starts with ChatGPT Pro ($100 per month) and Business and Enterprise plans, one Dot per user for now.
items.headline: OpenAI launches Dots, an always-on desktop agent

items.body: In an October 1 update, Neuralink said it trained self-supervised neural encoders on more than 50,000 hours of recordings from clinical trial participants. The approach cut calibration needs from about 10 minutes per day to 10 minutes per week for some participants. One participant set a BCI cursor-control record of 11.32 bits per second, which Neuralink says exceeds most able-bodied performance, a comparison not yet independently verified.
items.headline: Neuralink sets 11.32 bits-per-second BCI record

items.body: Microsoft's 2026 Digital Defense Report finds the median time from vulnerability discovery to weaponization is now well below 24 hours, while enterprises still take 30 to 60 days to fix critical externally facing flaws. Nearly 40,000 CVEs were published in the first half of 2026.
items.headline: Microsoft: exploits now arrive in under a day

items.body: Apple announced it will require explicit user action before apps can read the full filesystem, messages, and browsing history, citing the risks of increasingly autonomous AI agents. It is a platform-level response to the same agent capability trend OpenAI is pushing with Dots.
items.headline: Apple tightens Full Disk Access, citing AI agent risks

items.body: DeepSeek is in talks to raise about 50 billion yuan in its first external investment round, which would value the company at roughly 500 billion yuan. The raise comes the same week DeepSeek announced a partnership with Huawei to develop AI software and demonstrated its model running on Huawei chips.
items.headline: DeepSeek in talks for first external raise at $70B-equivalent valuation
OpenAI is in a governance crisis: three safety staff fired, GPT-6.1 Astra launch scrapped, and 50 petabytes of data under review.
Anthropic heads for a potential record IPO while its own filing warns of existential risk.
Agents move onto the desktop: OpenAI's Dots drive apps in a VM while Apple locks down filesystem permissions.
Neuralink's 50,000-hour pretraining cut BCI calibration to 10 minutes a week and set a cursor-control record.
Defenders lose the speed race: working exploits appear within a day while patching takes one to two months.
DeepSeek's first external raise marks China's open-model push catching up in capital terms.

editions.theme: The day's theme is accountability and control: labs are policing their own safety staff and warning investors about their models in SEC filings, agents are taking over desktops while Apple locks down permissions, and Microsoft confirms defenders now lose the speed race to attackers measured in hours.
